title: Progressive deploy guardrails: automated eval thresholds and rollback orchestration
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: We need a low-friction system that ties automated evaluation results to progressive model/config deployments. Current rollouts rely on manual checks and ad-hoc dashboards; this PRD aims to create a repeatable pipeline that gates canary and A/B deployments on eval-based quality signals and executes automated rollback when regressions exceed configured tolerances.

Goals:
- Define a canonical set of eval signals (accuracy, hallucination rate, safety score, latency regression, distributional drift) that can be mapped to rollout gates.
- Implement a rollout controller that consumes metrics and decides pass/fail per cohort in near real-time (target decision latency < 2 minutes).
- Provide an ergonomic config schema for teams to specify gate definitions, thresholds, comparison baselines (pinned model, historical rolling window), and rollback actions.
- Ensure observability: per-gate timelines, evidence traces, and post-mortem artifacts are stored and linkable to PRs.

Non-goals:
- Model retraining automation.
- Full integration with every third-party evaluation provider at launch.

Success criteria (high level):
- New rollouts using the system automatically block or rollback when an eval gate trips in >=95% of simulated failure scenarios in staging.
- Average time-to-detect a quality regression during canary runs < 3 minutes.
- Less than 10% of rollouts require manual intervention in the first month post-launch.

Design sketch:
1) Eval ingestion: existing eval-harness produces per-batch metrics to metrics ingestion topic (kafka: eval-results). Each message tags model_version, route, cohort, and config hash.
2) Gate engine: lightweight service (rollout-evaluator) reads eval-results, computes windowed aggregates (p50/p75/p95 latency, mean quality score, regression delta vs baseline), and evaluates rules defined in YAML policy files.
3) Decision plane: rollout-controller orchestrates traffic splits (canary->50%->full) and calls evaluator for each step. On a gate failure, controller executes rollback steps (immediate traffic reweight to baseline and submit a rollback event to audit log).
4) Evidence capture: when a gate trips, a compact evidence bundle (sample prompts, model outputs, metric deltas, commit ids) is persisted to S3 and linked in the rollout record.

Gate config example (user-facing):
- gate_name: "safety-smoke"
  metric: "safety_score.delta"
  comparator: "<= -0.03"
  window: "30m"
  baseline: "pinned:model@v12"
  action: "rollback"

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Real-time vs batch: streaming decisions are faster but add complexity; we'll start with 1-minute sliding windows to balance latency and compute cost.
- Baseline selection: allow pinned model and rolling historical baseline; define a safe default.
- False positives: strict thresholds reduce user risk but may increase rollbacks; include a vote/quorum mechanism for multi-metric gates.

Security/privacy considerations:
- Evidence bundles must redact PII by default. Eval-harness will flag prompts containing sensitive tokens and replace them with placeholders before persisting.
- Rollout events and audit logs respect RBAC and retention policies.

Operational plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): implement evaluator + controller integration, run synthetic failure tests and adversarial evals.
- Phase 2 (internal canaries): use for non-critical internal routes, collect metrics and tune thresholds.
- Phase 3 (public canaries): opt-in customers and dedicated capacity; watch rollback rates.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Progressive+Deploy+Guardrails
- Eval harness RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QzExample
- Prototype PR (evaluator + controller): https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/2115
- Monitoring dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/rollout-eval
acceptance_criteria: rollout-evaluator service deployed to staging and consumes eval-results topic
rollout-controller can reweight traffic automatically and perform rollback action when gate is flagged
evidence bundles are stored and linked in rollout records with PII redaction applied
integration tests simulate 20% quality drop and trigger rollback in >=95% of runs
comments: 2026-02-14 - Ava Martinez: Initial spike completed. PoC can evaluate p95 latency and a simple accuracy delta. Findings: 1-minute windows smooth noise but miss very short-lived regressions.
2026-02-24 - Sylvia Chen (Design): Reviewed the evidence UI mockups. Request: include an expandable sample list with fuzzy-diff highlighting for outputs that changed qualitatively.

2026-02-28 - Ravi Kapoor: Implemented initial gate YAML parser and Kafka consumer. Pushed prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/compare/rollout-eval-proto. Needs reviews on failure mode handling.
2026-03-03 - Security (Darren Lin): Confirmed PII redaction requirement and provided a small lib for token patterns. Will follow up with DAST for evidence storage flows.
2026-03-05 - QA (Melina Ortiz): Created test harness that injects synthetic eval messages. Passing local integration tests. Next: run adversarial prompts in staging.
2026-03-09 - PM (Caroline Vega): Prioritization review: move this to P1 for next cycle given several recent incidents where manual rollbacks cost time. Approved limited-scope public pilot.
notes: Consider adding a canary 'cooldown' period where the system waits 30m after a minor gate failure before forcing rollback, allowing transient flakiness to clear.
We should provide a CLI and Console UX for teams to preview how a proposed gate would have behaved against historical eval data (backtest).
If multiple gates conflict (one allows, one blocks), default to the most restrictive action unless teams opt into a quorum policy.
